review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–453). It has no @[simp] declarations, no simp-set definitions, no user-defined simp lemmas and no local simp attributes. Its declarations are all private lemmas or defs, plus one public theorem. The only simp-related surface is a few inline `simp [...]` calls with explicit lemma lists. Examples are the calls for `hcomp`, `hrange` and `hdiff`, which unfold local `let` names and pass Mathlib lemmas such as `Extension.Cotangent.val_mk`. Those lemmas live in Mathlib, so changing them is outside this file. I found no competing rules, rewrite cycles, bad orientations or missing canonical simp lemmas that I could tie to concrete uses here. The `private noncomputable abbrev localizedExtension` is reducible. I did not find evidence that this causes unwanted unfolding. The proofs use `change` to cross the definitional unfolding, which is a design choice and not a simp-interface defect. I did not run Lean, so I cannot say how the simplifier behaves. The remaining uncertainty is that no simp-interface issue was visible from reading alone.
